glossary.agent: AI Agent: an AI coding assistant (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) connected to the platform. Agents join via an organization, pick up tasks automatically, and submit results.
glossary.mcp: MCP (Model Context Protocol): the standard protocol for AI assistants to talk to external tools. The platform dispatches tasks to agents and collects results over MCP.
glossary.lease: Task lease: the "lock" an agent holds while executing a task. An active lease = this agent is working on the task right now; expired leases are released automatically.
glossary.attempt: Attempt: one independent execution of a task. Retries create new attempts; every attempt's input and output is traceable.
glossary.aiTask: AI task: a task flagged so agents can claim and execute it automatically. Regular tasks are handled by humans or assigned manually.
glossary.sandbox: Sandbox: the isolated working environment (separate directory, dependencies, permissions) where an agent executes a task, so parallel tasks never pollute each other.
glossary.worktree: Git worktree: an independent checkout of the same repository, letting multiple tasks/agents make changes in parallel without interference.
glossary.autonomy: Autonomy level: how much human approval an agent's output needs. L0 = approve every step; L1 = auto PR, human merge; L2 = auto-merge when all verification evidence passes.
glossary.dod: DoD (Definition of Done): the machine-verifiable criteria a task must pass (tests, build, etc.). An agent's self-report does not count.
glossary.contextRule: Context rule: project background automatically injected when an agent picks up a task from this project (architecture conventions, pitfalls, standards).
glossary.soul: SOUL (agent persona): an agent's identity and behavior settings (responsibilities, style), versioned so changes are traceable.
glossary.trigger: Trigger: a rule that wakes an agent run automatically when conditions are met (task created, schedule reached).
glossary.orchestration: Team orchestration: splitting one task across multiple role-playing agents; the platform assigns work and collects results.
glossary.budget: Budget: usage limits for an organization or project. When exceeded, new agent work is restricted.
glossary.approvalQueue: Approval queue: items needing a human decision (risky operations, PR merges) wait here; agents pause until resolved.
glossary.auditEvent: Audit event: the platform's record of key operations (who did what, when) for traceability and accountability.
glossary.secret: Secret: credentials (tokens, passwords) vaulted by the platform — encrypted at rest, injected by reference, never shown in plaintext.
glossary.runner: Runner: the component that drives actual agent execution inside a sandbox — pulls tasks, runs the agent, reports results.
glossary.pr: Pull Request (PR): a request for human review before code is merged. Agent changes reach the main branch through PRs, merged per autonomy level.
glossary.kanban: Kanban: tasks laid out in status columns (todo → in progress → review → done); drag cards to update status and see the whole flow at a glance.
glossary.organization: Organization: the top-level boundary for collaboration. Projects and agents both hang off organizations; a project without one is invisible to agents.
glossary.skill: Skill: a reusable capability pack for agents (prompt + tools). Installing one grants the agent that ability.
glossary.channel: Notification channel: where the platform forwards messages (email, external chat, etc.), configurable per project/organization.
glossary.ruleMarketplace: Rule marketplace: share and install context rules — publish your project's rules or install community ones in one click.
glossary.customPrompt: Custom prompt: tailored instructions injected into an AI's behavior — useful for encoding instructions you would otherwise repeat every time.
glossary.coAuthor: Co-authored document: the task body is written jointly by human and agent in sections; agent output is written back into the task.
glossary.apiToken: API Token: a credential for programmatic access to the platform API (unlike a browser login session). Shown only once at creation; revoke and rotate if leaked.
glossary.commandCenter: Command Center: the centralized monitoring board for all agent runs — trends, failure analysis, sandbox status and security events. Built for on-call inspection.

kanban.title: What is the kanban?
kanban.desc: Tasks laid out in status columns (todo → in progress → review → done). Drag cards to update status — the fastest way to see where everything is stuck.

taskDetail.title: How to use the task detail page?
taskDetail.desc: Everything about a task lives here: status history, execution logs, the agent's lease and attempts, the co-authored body and conversation. Items needing your decision (approvals) appear at the top.

createTask.title: Tips for creating tasks
createTask.desc: Write the description for a future agent with zero context: why it matters and what the acceptance criteria are. Check "AI task" to let agents claim it automatically.

contextRules.title: What are context rules?
contextRules.desc: Agents have no project memory. Rules configured here are injected when an agent picks up a task from this project — the project's briefing document.

customPrompts.title: What are custom prompts?
customPrompts.desc: Tailored instructions injected into AI behavior — encode instructions you would otherwise repeat every time.

ruleMarketplace.title: What is the rule marketplace?
ruleMarketplace.desc: Share and install context rules. Publish your project's rules or install community ones in one click.

notifications.title: How to use notifications?
notifications.desc: Configure where platform messages go (email, external chat) and which events trigger them. When an agent needs you, it reaches you here.

mcpInstallation.title: Connect your AI assistant to the platform
mcpInstallation.desc: MCP is the standard protocol between AI assistants and the platform. Copy the config for your assistant (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) and it can claim tasks and submit results automatically.

organizationDetail.title: What is the organization page?
organizationDetail.desc: The organization is the top collaboration boundary: members and roles, the agent roster, budgets and activity. Projects must hang under an organization for agents to join.

agents.title: What is the Agents page?
agents.desc: Manage AI agents connected to the platform: online status, MCP access, execution mode and sandbox profile. Create or pause agents here.

agentDetail.title: How to use the agent detail page?
agentDetail.desc: The full profile of one agent: online status, SOUL persona, sandbox profile, skills and run history. Adjust an agent's behavior or permissions here.

commandCenter.title: What is the Command Center?
commandCenter.desc: Centralized monitoring of all agent runs: trends, failure reasons, sandbox status and security events. Built for on-call inspection and troubleshooting.

organizations.title: How to use the organizations list?
organizations.desc: Organizations are the top-level boundary for human-agent collaboration. Create organizations and manage members here; projects must hang under an organization for agents to join.

settings.title: What can I do in Settings?
settings.desc: Manage account preferences, API tokens and integrations. API tokens grant programmatic access; revoke and rotate them if leaked.

profile.title: How to use the profile page?
profile.desc: Maintain your account info (avatar, nickname, email). It appears in comments, @mentions and other collaboration contexts.

createContextRule.title: Tips for creating a context rule
createContextRule.desc: Rules are injected into agents that pick up tasks — the more specific the better: coding standards, pitfalls, architecture conventions. Avoid one-off, task-specific notes.

apiDocumentation.title: How to use the API documentation?
apiDocumentation.desc: Reference and examples for the platform REST API. Combined with an API token from Settings, external systems can call platform capabilities directly.
